## Worksheet 3, P2 — Penguins

<br>

**The Model:**
$$\hat{y} = 389.6 + 49.2x$$

where $x$ = flipper length (mm) and $\hat{y}$ = predicted body mass (g)

Data range: 172–231 mm

<br>

**Key Interpretation:**

[Slope (49.2):]{.teal} for **1 mm increase** in flipper length, body mass increases by 49.2 g on average

[Change is what matters:]{.gold style="font-weight: 600;"} Δŷ = slope × Δx &nbsp;·&nbsp; we don't need the actual x value, only the change

---

## Extrapolation Warning

<br>

Generally speaking, do **NOT** apply a model to data that lies outside of what the model was fit on.

<br>

**Two critical factors:**

1. [Range of data:]{.teal} was the x value in your data? (penguins: 172–231 mm) → don't predict for 20 mm

2. [Who was sampled:]{.teal} what population is the model for? → don't use a penguin model for hawks

## Multiplication Rule


General rule is (works for dependent case):

$$P(A \text{ and } B) = {\color{#E5A823}{P(A \mid B)}} \times P(B)$$

If independent, knowing $B$ doesn't change $P(A)$ so... ${\color{#E5A823}{P(A \mid B)}} = {\color{#E5A823}{P(A)}}$.

If independent:

$$P(A \text{ and } B) = {\color{#E5A823}{P(A)}} \times P(B).$$

## Common Misconception

[Mutually exclusive]{.teal} ≠ [independent]{.gold}

- [Mutually exclusive]{.teal} means the two events cannot both happen i.e.

$$P(A \text{ and } B) = 0$$

- [Independent]{.gold} means knowing $A$ doesn't change $P(B)$ so,

$$P(A \mid B) = P(A)$$.


---

## Conditional Probability: The Formula

<br>

[Start with the multiplication rule:]{.teal}

$$P(A \text{ and } B) = {\color{#E5A823}{P(A \mid B)}} \times P(B)$$


[Rearrange to solve for]{.teal} ${\color{#E5A823}{P(A \mid B)}}$:

$${\color{#E5A823}{P(A \mid B)}} = \frac{P(A \text{ and } B)}{P(B)}$$

## FR1 (a) — Interpreting the Intercept

$\hat{y} = 3.55 + 0.38x$ &nbsp;&nbsp; (weight in lbs → diastolic BP in mmHg)

Data range: 178–267 lbs

<br>

**Is it appropriate to interpret 3.55?**

[No — NOT appropriate]{.gold}

The intercept would be: predicted BP when weight = 0 lbs

- Weight of 0 lbs is [impossible]{.teal}
- It's [far outside]{.teal} the data range (178–267 lbs)
- This would be [extrapolation]{.gold}

---

## FR1 (b) — Using for Fourth Graders

**Should we use this model to predict BP for fourth graders?**

[No]{.gold}

- Model was fit on [middle-aged men]{.teal} weighing 178–267 lbs
- Fourth graders are a [different population]{.teal}
- Their weights (~60–100 lbs) [fall outside the training range]{.gold}
- Applying it would be [extrapolation]{.gold}

---

## FR1 (c) — Change in Prediction

**Alonzo weighs 190–210 lbs. He loses 20 pounds. What's the predicted change in BP?**

<br>

Use the formula: Δŷ = slope × Δx

$$\Delta\hat{y} = 0.38 \times (-20) = -7.60 \text{ mmHg}$$

<br>

**Interpretation:** Losing 20 lbs is associated with a predicted **decrease of 7.60 mmHg** in diastolic BP

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7);"}
Note: We only need the change in x, not his exact weight
:::

---

```{=html}
    <td style="padding: 0.3em 0.6em; text-align: center; color: #E5A823;">677</td>
    <td style="padding: 0.3em 0.6em; text-align: center; color: #E5A823; font-weight:600;">20,000</td>
  </tr>
</table>
```

<br>

**Question:** P(excellent health **AND** no coverage)?

<br>

[Use joint: cell ÷ grand total]{.teal}

$$P(\text{excellent AND no coverage}) = \frac{459}{20,000}$$

---

## FR2 (b) — Addition Rule

**Question:** P(excellent health **OR** no coverage)?

<br>

[Use addition rule:]{.teal}

$$P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B)$$

$$P(\text{excellent OR no coverage}) = \frac{4,657}{20,000} + \frac{2,524}{20,000} - \frac{459}{20,000} = \frac{6,722}{20,000}$$

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.80em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.6);"}
Remember to subtract the intersection — don't double-count the 459
:::

---

## FR2 (c) — Conditional Probability

**Question:** P(excellent health, **given** no coverage)?

<br>

[Use conditional: "given no coverage" → restrict to that row]{.teal}

$$P(\text{excellent | no coverage}) = \frac{459}{2,524}$$

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.80em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.6);"}
The denominator is the row total (2,524), not the grand total (20,000)
:::
